findings.title: loadOptional silently swallows ALL import errors — silent skip masks real regressions
findings.explanation: The helper used by all 22 phase-1/3/4/6 gates wraps `await import(path)` in a bare `try {} catch { return null; }` with no error type discrimination and no logging. This means: (a) a module-not-found error returns null (the intended case), but also (b) a TypeScript-compile error in the imported module returns null (silent skip), (c) a runtime exception in the module's top-level returns null (silent skip), (d) a circular-import deadlock returns null (silent skip). Once the gated modules exist (and they all do), this helper's only effect is to convert build/runtime regressions into green skipped tests. The companion `describe.skipIf(!module)` then hides the failure.
findings.proposed_action: Either (preferred) delete `loadOptional` and all `describe.skipIf` gates entirely now that Phase 1/3/4/6 have shipped, OR narrow the catch to a typed module-not-found check (e.g. `if (err.code !== 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND' && !err.message.includes('Failed to resolve')) throw err`). Add a CI guard that fails if `loadOptional` is reintroduced for any of the four shipped paths.

findings.title: All `(deferred)` describe blocks with phase-N it.todo placeholders are dead
findings.explanation: 15 `describe.skipIf(<module>)('… (deferred)', () => { it.todo('phase-N: <module> not yet present') })` blocks exist purely as placeholders for the case where the gated module is missing. Each gated module is now present. The describe blocks: (a) never run (skipIf is true), (b) carry no executable assertions, (c) reference completed phases. They are pure documentation of completed work — the kind the project's `.claude/rules/comments.md` rule explicitly flags ("No comments mentioning refactors / cleanups — 'no longer', 'phase', 'removed', 'deleted', 'deprecated', 'legacy', 'old', 'new', 'will change/be' etc. are red flags, don't include and clean them up if you come across them"). Counterpart at the file level: this rule applies to test code too.
findings.proposed_action: Delete all 15 `(deferred)` describe blocks in the same change that removes the `describe.skipIf` gates. They are dead placeholders for completed phases.
findings.verifier_notes: All 15 cited files contain `describe.skipIf(MODULE)('... (deferred)', () => { it.todo(...) })` blocks where MODULE is now a loaded module (truthy value). When MODULE is truthy, `skipIf(truthy)` skips execution—these blocks never run. Verified: registry.ts, apply-command.ts, identity.ts, stale.ts, resolve-issue.ts, chapter.ts, and segments.ts all exist at their import paths. Each deferred block contains only an `it.todo()` placeholder with no executable assertions. The `.claude/rules/comments.md` rule explicitly states phase mentions are red flags in comments and should be removed. These are pure documentation of completed phases (phase-1 through phase-6) with zero test value. They violate the project's own cleanup rule.

findings.title: pytest.skip on missing on-disk fixture is justified
findings.explanation: The only backend `pytest.skip()` is `if not fixture_path.is_file(): pytest.skip(f"fixture missing: {fixture_path}")`. Both parametrized fixtures (`112-ikhlas.detailed.json`, `113-falaq.detailed.json`) currently exist on disk, so the skip never fires. The guard is defensive (protects against running tests in environments where fixtures were not synced) and the skip message is informative. Justified — though arguably could be tightened to a hard failure since these fixtures are checked into the repo and should always be present.
findings.proposed_action: Leave as-is, or tighten to `assert fixture_path.is_file(), f"fixture missing: {fixture_path}"` for stronger CI signal (committed fixtures should be present unconditionally). Low priority.
findings.verifier_notes: The skip on missing fixtures (test_segment_schema.py:260-261) is defensive but unnecessary. Both parametrized fixtures (112-ikhlas.detailed.json and 113-falaq.detailed.json) are committed to the repo and will always be present during test execution. CI runs `python -m pytest` with no fixture-sync step, so pytest collects both parametrized test cases and the skip condition never fires. The test docstring labels the section "optional" but this reflects the original design intent before fixtures were committed. Since fixtures are now part of the repo, the skip's defensive posture is outdated. The reviewer's proposed action to replace with `assert fixture_path.is_file()` is justified — committed files should fail hard if missing rather than silently skip, providing clearer CI signal on repo integrity. Low priority as the test works correctly today, but tightening to assert is the right fix.

findings.title: behavior.test.ts mixes throw-inside-it AND describe.skipIf for the same module

findings.title: CI guard only catches schemas.ts drift, not 'fe_types.py is missing a model the FE consumes'
findings.explanation: scripts/codegen/regen_fe_types.py walks SCHEMAS_MODULE = 'qua_shared.schemas.fe_types' — only models re-exported there land in inspector/frontend/src/lib/types/generated/schemas.ts. The schema-codegen-check CI job runs the same regen and `git diff --exit-code`s schemas.ts, so it catches 'forgot to regen', but NOT 'added a new model to qua_shared/schemas/X.py + a new FE consumer, but never added it to fe_types.py'. Evidence of this risk landing live: inspector/frontend/src/lib/api/requests.ts:26 hand-rolls `export interface PendingRequest` even though qua_shared/schemas/pending_requests.py::PendingRequest exists in the canonical schema set — but it's NOT in fe_types.py (only EditHistoryBatch/EditOperation are re-exported from edit_history). Alternative: add a guard that compares qua_shared.schemas.__all__ ∩ {models the FE actually imports} ⊆ fe_types.__all__, or invert the convention so fe_types.py re-exports the full set and the codegen runs against qua_shared.schemas directly. This creates a drift vulnerability. However, the evidence about TsValidationDoc/Meta/Verse is inaccurate — these ARE properly exported from fe_types.py and properly imported by the FE. findings.title: smoke.py constructs EditHistoryBatch/EditOperation with fields the schema silently strips — passes for the wrong reason
findings.explanation: smoke.py line 236 does EditHistoryBatch(..., ts=_now(), ...), but the schema (edit_history.py:120) declares saved_at_utc, NOT ts. With extra='forbid' + strip_and_warn pre-validator, `ts` is warn-stripped silently during construction. Likewise line 240 EditOperation(op_id=..., kind='trim', new_end=1.234) — `new_end` is not a declared EditOperation field (only op_id/kind/op_type/fix_kind/targets_before/targets_after). Both fields disappear. _round_trip() then compares `reparsed != model`, but both sides equally lack the stripped fields, so the assertion passes despite the test never actually exercising a ts/new_end persistence path. If someone fixes smoke.py to use saved_at_utc, the round-trip would still pass — but the warning logs emitted during construction reveal that the AUTHOR intent (smoke-test that real Inspector save shapes round-trip) is unmet today.
findings.proposed_action: If smoke.py is kept (see schemas-smoke-not-in-ci), rewrite the EditHistoryBatch/EditOperation construction to use the canonical Migration #5 fields (saved_at_utc, op_type, targets_before, targets_after). Add an explicit caplog assertion that NO WARNING-level strip_and_warn message fires during construction of a well-formed model — to catch future drift between smoke and schema.
findings.verifier_notes: The smoke test at qua_shared/schemas/smoke.py:234-240 constructs EditHistoryBatch with ts field and EditOperation with new_end field. However, the schema (edit_history.py:120, line 136) declares only saved_at_utc, and EditOperation (edit_history.py lines 77-84) declares only op_id/kind/op_type/fix_kind/targets_before/targets_after. The strip_and_warn pre-validator logs WARNING messages ('ts' and 'new_end' as unrecognized fields) and strips them. The _round_trip() test passes because both original and reparsed objects equally lack these fields, not because the schema correctly preserved them. Running the smoke test produces the warnings: 'EditHistoryBatch: stripped UNRECOGNIZED field(s) [ts]' and 'EditOperation: stripped UNRECOGNIZED field(s) [new_end]'. The test never exercises persistence of ts/new_end. ts should either be added to _BATCH_DEAD_FIELDS (if truly legacy) or the smoke test should use the canonical saved_at_utc field; new_end should not be used at all. A caplog assertion would catch future drift.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md says schemas use ConfigDict(extra='allow') for forward-compat — but the persistence schemas use extra='forbid' + strip_and_warn (opposite behavior)
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md's Conventions section states: 'Shared schemas live in qua_shared/schemas/ (Pydantic v2, ConfigDict(extra="allow") for forward-compat).' This is correct for admin_*/intake/mark_ready/ts_validation/playlist_map but is the OPPOSITE of what edit_history, peaks_history, segment (DetailedSegment + DetailedEntry), and AudioManifestSidecar (+ nested) actually do. Those use extra='forbid' plus a strip_and_warn pre-validator that DROPS unknown fields with a warn log (per _extras.py:1 docstring). The doc claim plus the behaviour mismatch will mislead an agent into assuming a writer ahead of the reader is safe — but for any persistence schema, an unknown future field WILL be stripped on read and lost on rewrite.
findings.proposed_action: Update CLAUDE.md to distinguish (a) wire/admin response models (extra='allow', forward-compat preserved) from (b) on-disk persistence models (extra='forbid' + strip_and_warn, dead/unknown stripped). Reference _extras.py and the warn-then-strip behaviour. Cross-link from the schema convention to docs/reference/data-migrations.md §5.
findings.verifier_notes: CLAUDE.md:137 claims "Shared schemas live in qua_shared/schemas/ (Pydantic v2, ConfigDict(extra='allow') for forward-compat)" but persistence schemas (edit_history.py:75,116; peaks_history.py:65; segment.py:97,152,177,216; catalog.py:63,87,103,110,123,143,198,210,218,227,308,318,336) all use extra='forbid' + strip_and_warn pre-validator (documented in _extras.py:1). Wire/admin models use extra='allow', but persistence models use the opposite pattern: extra='forbid' with strip-then-warn that DROPS unknown fields. This distinction is critical because it means unknown future fields are lost on read/rewrite, not preserved. The claim directly contradicts both the code behavior and _extras.py's explicit design rationale.

findings.title: _OP_DEAD_FIELDS / _BATCH_DEAD_FIELDS have no automated cross-check against the real writers
findings.explanation: _OP_DEAD_FIELDS and _BATCH_DEAD_FIELDS are hand-curated sets ('audit survey, May 2026' per the comment) intended to silently absorb known-legacy keys with INFO instead of WARNING logs. There is no test that asserts these sets are a STRICT SUPERSET of the keys actually present in fixtures (inspector/tests/fixtures/segments/*.detailed.json or any committed edit_history.jsonl sample). When a writer (the offline pipeline at .local/extraction/segments/post_passes.py) starts emitting a new payload key for a feature, the reader will surface it as a WARNING — which is the intent — but if the dev forgets to add the legacy mapping, future fixtures will start firing WARN logs in unrelated tests, polluting CI signal.
findings.proposed_action: Add a one-shot test that loads every committed edit_history.jsonl sample (in fixtures), feeds each line through parse_edit_history_line + captures caplog, and asserts caplog.records has zero WARNING entries — only INFO (legacy strips). Any new WARN must be classified by the dev as 'declared field' or 'legacy strip' before merge.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding is real. No test currently loads the committed fixture edit_history.jsonl files and validates they parse with zero WARNING logs. The fixture at inspector/tests/fixtures/segments/112-ikhlas.edit_history.jsonl contains legacy fields (reciter, save_mode, file_hash_after, type, started_at_utc, applied_at_utc, ready_at_utc) that parse successfully with INFO logs only. However, smoke test uses unrecognized fields (ts, new_end) that generate WARN logs but don't check caplog. ---
# testing.md — outline

## 1. Scope & quick map
- One-paragraph: BE pytest tree under `inspector/tests/`, FE vitest tree colocated as `src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts`, shared fixtures under `inspector/tests/fixtures/segments/` (aliased to `@fixtures` in vitest).
- Pointer table: subsystem → test dir (mirrors the docs/reference/README.md table):
  - state-machine → `inspector/tests/db/test_repo_transitions.py`, `services/test_state_request_events.py`
  - database / repos → `inspector/tests/db/test_repo_*.py`, `test_sync.py`, `test_durability.py`, `test_migration.py`
  - auth / capabilities → `inspector/tests/services/test_capabilities.py`, `test_permissions.py`, `test_auth_oauth_state.py`, `tests/test_capability_convention.py`
  - admin dashboard → `inspector/tests/admin/`, `tests/routes/test_route_access_admin.py`, `test_route_admin_actions.py`
  - HTTP routes → `inspector/tests/routes/test_route_*.py`
  - segments editor (BE) → `inspector/tests/command/`, `tests/undo/`, `tests/persistence/`, `tests/parity/`
  - validation → `inspector/tests/classifier/`, `tests/registry/`, `tests/services/test_missed_basmala_rule.py`, `test_tajweed.py`
  - audio / peaks / VBR → `inspector/tests/test_peaks_*.py`, `test_ts_vbr.py`, `test_audio_meta.py`, `test_audio_source.py`, `tests/routes/test_route_audio_proxy.py`, `test_route_peaks.py`
  - timestamps job → `inspector/tests/services/test_timestamps_jobs.py`, `tests/routes/test_route_generate_timestamps.py`
  - dataset / releases → `inspector/tests/db/test_repo_releases.py`, `tests/routes/test_route_admin_releases.py`
  - FE segments editor → `inspector/frontend/src/tabs/segments/__tests__/`
  - FE timestamps → `inspector/frontend/src/tabs/timestamps/__tests__/`
  - FE lib (playback, components, stores, utils) → `inspector/frontend/src/lib/**/__tests__/`

## 2. Test runners & tools
- BE: pytest, single autouse `_substrate_db` fixture (conftest.py:117) gives every test a fresh migrated SQLite + sync disabled; teardown resets db_seq + caches.
- FE: vitest (`vitest run` / `vitest --coverage`), `happy-dom` env, `@testing-library/svelte` for component mounting + `@testing-library/user-event`, `vitest.setup.ts` for global stubs.
- Shared seeding primitives: `_seed_delivery_chain`, `_seed_state`, `_seed_catalog`, `_seed_role` (all module-level in conftest.py:153-272 so other conftests can import).
- FilesystemBackend (services/hf_bucket.py) — pytest helpers `tmp_reciter_dir` and `state_persistence` install it via `monkeypatch.setenv` + `set_backend`; never hits a real bucket.
- signed_in_client factory mints a signed cookie via `auth_service.encode_session` so route tests can drive role-gated endpoints without OAuth.
- E2E: playwright (`npm run test:e2e`) — out of scope for this doc beyond a pointer.

## 3. Running tests
- BE all: `cd inspector && python -m pytest tests/ -v`
- BE single file: `python -m pytest tests/db/test_repo_state.py -v`
- BE single test: `python -m pytest tests/db/test_repo_state.py::test_name -v`
- BE keyword: `python -m pytest -k transition tests/`
- BE with coverage: `python -m pytest --cov=services --cov=routes --cov-report=term-missing tests/`
- FE all: `cd inspector/frontend && npm run test`
- FE watch: `npm run test:watch`
- FE single: `npx vitest run src/lib/playback/__tests__/audio-graph.test.ts`
- FE coverage: `npm run test:coverage` (v8 provider, HTML in `frontend/coverage/`)
- FE typecheck (separate from tests, required for CI parity): `npm run check`
- Note: CI does NOT gate on coverage thresholds (vitest.config.ts:31 `thresholds: undefined`); coverage is informational.

## 4. How to add a test for X subsystem — four walkthroughs

### 4a. State-machine transition rule (BE)
- File: `inspector/tests/db/test_repo_transitions.py` (transitions matrix) OR `inspector/tests/services/test_state_request_events.py` (events).
- Pattern: import `from services.state.state import transition`; use the `seed_state` fixture to set the FROM state, call `transition(slug, ...)`, assert returned `ReciterState` + that `repo_audit` has the expected row. Never mutate state ad-hoc — `transition()` is the only sanctioned entry per CLAUDE.md invariant.
- Fixture: `seed_state` (autouse `_substrate_db` makes it cheap).

### 4b. HTTP route handler (BE)
- File: add under `inspector/tests/routes/test_route_<name>.py`.
- Pattern: `client, user = signed_in_client(role="contributor")`; if the route reads/writes per-reciter bucket content, also request `tmp_reciter_dir` and call `tmp.install("<slug>", "<fixture>")` or `tmp.seed_under_review(<slug>, user["hf_user_id"])`; then `client.post("/api/...", json=..., headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})`. The Origin header is required for CSRF on mutating routes.
- Assert JSON shape + side-effects via `repo_*` reads, not via re-reading mocks.

### 4c. A segments editor command (FE + BE)
- FE side: add a `*.test.ts` under `inspector/frontend/src/tabs/segments/__tests__/command/` next to the existing `delete.test.ts`/`merge.test.ts`. Build state via `makeSegment` (in `__tests__/helpers/make-segment.ts`), call `applyCommand(state, command)` directly, assert `result.nextState` + `result.operation` shape. Do NOT use the phase-1 `loadOptional` + `describe.skipIf(!applyCommand)` wrapper for new tests — the module is present (see Section 7).
- BE side: `inspector/tests/command/` plus `tests/persistence/` for the JSONL round-trip; use `tmp_reciter_dir` to install a detailed.json fixture, POST to `/api/save/<slug>`, then read `repo_*` / FilesystemBackend.

### 4d. A frontend component
- File: `src/lib/components/__tests__/<Name>.test.ts`.
- Pattern (mirror `ClaimButton.test.ts`, `Modal.test.ts`): `import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/svelte'`; `render(Component, { props: { ... } })`; assert via `screen.getByRole`/`getByText`; for events use `@testing-library/user-event`'s `userEvent.setup()`. Svelte 5 components: pass `$bindable` props as plain values; the harness handles reactivity.
- For components reading stores: import the store, set state directly in the test, then render.

## 5. Fixture cheatsheet
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Just a SQLite DB | nothing (autouse `_substrate_db`) |
| Seed a state row + FK chain | `seed_state(slug, state=, assignee_hf_id=, marked_ready=, ...)` |
| Seed a member's role | `seed_role(hf_user_id, login=, role=)` |
| Mint a signed-in test client | `signed_in_client(role="...")` → `(client, user)` |
| Per-reciter content (bucket files) | `tmp_reciter_dir` — `.install(slug, fixture_name)`, `.seed_under_review(slug, hf_id)`, `.backend` (FilesystemBackend), `.data_dir` |
| Per-reciter content WITHOUT a fixture | `state_persistence` — wires FilesystemBackend + autouse SQLite, yields backend |
| Load a JSON fixture file | `load_fixture(name)` → dict from `tests/fixtures/segments/<name>.detailed.json` |
| Load a baseline expected output | `load_expected(name, kind)` |
| Validation registry snapshot | `fresh_registry` |
| Flask client without auth | `flask_client` |

Rule: don't reach for `tmp_reciter_dir` if all you need is SQLite state — the autouse fixture already gave you that.

## 6. Mocking cheatsheet
- **BE — bucket / data dir:** never patch `Path.read_text` or hf_bucket internals. Use `tmp_reciter_dir` or `state_persistence` — they install `FilesystemBackend` and set `INSPECTOR_BACKEND=filesystem`. Per the CLAUDE.md bucket-first convention all reads route through `services/storage/data_dir.py`, so swapping the backend covers every call site.
- **BE — env vars:** always `monkeypatch.setenv(...)`, never `os.environ[...] = ...`. The autouse SQLite reset is the only sanctioned global mutation.
- **BE — HF OAuth / identity:** use `signed_in_client(role=...)` — it seeds the user row + mints a signed cookie. Do not mock `auth_service.encode_session`.
- **BE — external HTTP (Quran Foundation, HF API):** use `monkeypatch` to patch the specific service function (e.g. `services/quran_foundation/...`), not `requests.get`. Stay one level above the transport.
- **BE — caches:** rely on the autouse teardown; if a new cache is added, register an invalidator in `services/storage/cache.py` (per the cache-via-getter/setter convention) and add it to the conftest teardown list (`conftest.py:138-150`, `_SEG_CACHE_NAMES`).
- **FE — modules:** prefer real imports + props-driven state over `vi.mock`. Use `vi.mock` only for ambient browser APIs (e.g. `window.fetch`, `AudioContext`) and shared singletons (the audio port). Mirror the existing pattern in `lib/playback/__tests__/audio-port.test.ts`.
- **FE — fetch:** `vi.spyOn(window, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue(new Response(JSON.stringify(...), { status: 200 }))`. Don't reach for MSW unless a multi-endpoint flow forces it.
- **FE — stores:** import the real store, set state before render. Mocking a store usually means the test is asserting the mock.

## 7. Phase-gate (`describe.skipIf`) policy
- Pattern in use: `tabs/segments/__tests__/command/*.test.ts` and `__tests__/helpers/optional.ts` use `loadOptional('../../domain/<module>')` + `describe.skipIf(!module)('...', ...)` / `describe.skipIf(module)('... (deferred)', it.todo(...))`. The intent was a phase-1 gate while the domain module was being landed.
- **When to add one:** ONLY when introducing a test for a module that does not yet exist on `main` and will land in a follow-up commit on the same branch series. Pair with a `it.todo('phase-N: <module> not yet present')` in the deferred branch.
- **When to remove one:** the moment the module lands. Today `tabs/segments/domain/apply-command.ts` exists, so every `describe.skipIf(!applyCommand)` / `describe.skipIf(applyCommand)` pair under `__tests__/command/` (apply-command, auto-suppress, delete, ignore, merge, reference, split, trim) is stale — drop the `loadOptional` wrapper, do a static `import { applyCommand } from '../../domain/apply-command'`, and delete the deferred `it.todo` block.
- Rule: a phase-gate older than the PR that introduced it is a smell. Audit on every command/* touch.

## 8. Schema parity policy (codegen)
- After ANY edit under `qua_shared/schemas/`: `python scripts/codegen/regen_fe_types.py` then commit `inspector/frontend/src/lib/types/generated/schemas.ts` in the same change.
- CI's `schema-codegen-check` job runs the same command + `git diff --exit-code`; it fails the build if the file is out of sync.
- Tests that round-trip artefacts (`detailed.json`, `edit_history.jsonl`, `edit_history_peaks.jsonl`, audio-manifest sidecars) MUST construct objects via the Pydantic models (e.g. `PipelineMeta(...)` in `tmp_reciter_dir._install`, conftest.py:489-495), never dict literals — this is the writer/reader-drift guard.
- Add a round-trip test under `inspector/tests/persistence/` for every new schema (BE-side construction → write → bucket read → reparse).

## 9. Coverage how-to
- BE local: `cd inspector && python -m pytest --cov=services --cov=routes --cov=domain --cov=adapters --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html tests/`. HTML at `inspector/htmlcov/`.
- FE local: `cd inspector/frontend && npm run test:coverage`. HTML at `inspector/frontend/coverage/`.
- CI does not gate on thresholds (vitest.config.ts:31 `thresholds: undefined`); coverage is informational, used for spotting unreached subsystems, not blocking PRs.
- Don't game coverage with assertion-free smoke tests — the audit will flag them as `dead-test`.

## 10. Conventions (terse, last)
- Test name pattern: `test_<unit>_<scenario>_<expectation>` for BE; `it('does X when Y', ...)` for FE. Opaque names like `test_basic` are a smell — audit category=naming.
- Co-locate FE tests under `__tests__/` alongside the unit under test. Co-locate BE tests under the subpackage that mirrors the prod tree (`tests/services/`, `tests/routes/`, `tests/db/`).
- One conftest per major tree; promote any duplicated seeder up to `inspector/tests/conftest.py`.
- Add a one-line row to docs/reference/README.md when this doc lands.

findings.title: Zero accessibility tests across the FE suite — no axe, no aria assertions on the core interactive surface
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/__tests__/Toggle.test.ts:8-28 (only file in the suite that asserts a `role="switch"`, `aria-checked`, and Enter/Space keyboard activation)
findings.explanation: Of the ~73 frontend test files, exactly one (Toggle.test.ts) makes any genuine a11y assertion (role + aria-checked + Space/Enter). No axe-core or jest-axe is installed, so no test computes an accessibility tree or fails on a violation. The chrome-devtools-mcp:a11y-debugging guidelines (semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus states, keyboard nav, tap targets, contrast) have no representation in CI — regressions in any of these will not be caught.
findings.proposed_action: Add `@axe-core/svelte` (or jest-axe equivalent for vitest + happy-dom) as a dev dep. Author a shared `assertNoA11yViolations(container)` helper used by every component-level `*.test.ts`. Treat a violation in any rendered subtree as a test failure. Also introduce a single "a11y smoke" file that mounts the top-level shells (App, AdminDashboardModal, ValidationPanel, CombinationPicker, SegmentsTab) and runs axe against each in a default and dark-theme variant.

findings.title: SearchableSelect combobox has no tests at all despite implementing custom keyboard navigation
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/SearchableSelect.svelte:1-11 (docstring: "filterable dropdown with keyboard navigation (arrows, Enter, Escape) and Arabic text normalization")
inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/SearchableSelect.svelte:71-100 (onKey handler implements ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Enter / Escape with preventDefault)
inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/__tests__/ (directory listing: ClaimButton, ClaimConfirmModal, EditAffordancePopover, Modal, SearchInput, Toggle — no SearchableSelect.test.ts)
findings.explanation: SearchableSelect is a custom combobox that hand-rolls ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Enter / Escape navigation, highlight tracking, scroll-to-highlight, and Arabic-normalized fuzzy filtering — exactly the kind of widget where ARIA combobox semantics and keyboard nav silently regress. The repo reaches for it in pickers and admin forms but the entire component has zero unit tests, let alone a11y assertions for `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`, or `aria-controls`. Right now the only ARIA in source is one `role="button"` on a clear icon (line 131).
findings.proposed_action: Add SearchableSelect.test.ts: render with options → assert input has `role="combobox"` and `aria-expanded` toggles on focus/close; ArrowDown moves highlight and updates `aria-activedescendant`; Enter selects the highlighted option and dispatches `change`; Escape closes and restores prior label; type queries filter the listbox. Promote the static role/aria attributes onto the markup as part of the fix.

findings.title: Modal focus trap and focus-return are implemented but no test verifies them
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/Modal.svelte:28-45 (`manageOpen` snapshots `document.activeElement` and restores it on close)
inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/Modal.svelte:76-98 (Tab / Shift+Tab cycling between first and last focusable elements)
inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/__tests__/Modal.test.ts:38-46 (only covers Escape close, backdrop click, body scroll lock — no Tab cycle, no focus return, no role/aria assertion)
findings.explanation: The dialog primitive used by every modal in the app implements four a11y contracts — autofocus first element, focus-trap on Tab and Shift+Tab, focus-return to the previously focused element on close, and the dialog role/aria-modal/aria-label trio. The test file asserts none of these. Anyone refactoring `getFocusable()` or removing `previouslyFocused.focus()` will not see a failure. Because dozens of modals (Sign-in, Claim, AdminDashboard, MarkReady, CutRelease, AccordionGuide, GuidesGate, ClaimConfirm) inherit from this shell, the regression blast radius is the entire dialog surface.
findings.proposed_action: Extend Modal.test.ts: (1) assert the dialog root has `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and the expected `aria-label`; (2) render with a previously-focused element in the body and assert it regains focus on close; (3) render with multiple focusable children and assert Tab from the last cycles to the first, and Shift+Tab from the first cycles to the last; (4) assert focusFirst lands on the first non-disabled focusable.

findings.title: Validation accordion lacks aria-expanded/aria-controls in source and has no keyboard nav test
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/tabs/segments/components/validation/ValidationPanel.svelte:818 (only ARIA usage in the file: `aria-label={\`Open guide for ${cat.name}\`}`)
inspector/frontend/src/tabs/segments/components/validation/ValidationPanel.svelte:890,902 (the other two ARIA usages: `aria-hidden="true"` on virtualization spacers)
findings.explanation: The validation panel is the primary editor-facing surface — a long accordion-style list of category cards with expand/collapse interactions. Source has zero `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` / `aria-selected` attributes (grep returns 0). Tests do not exist for the panel itself: no Tab between accordion headers, no Enter/Space to expand, no aria-expanded toggling, no focus on the expanded section. Screen-reader users currently cannot perceive expand state at all, and there is no test that would prevent the panel from regressing further.
findings.proposed_action: Step 1 (fix source — separate PR): add `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `role="region"` / `aria-labelledby` to accordion headers and panels. Step 2 (test): add ValidationPanel.test.ts that asserts each header has `role="button"` and `aria-expanded`, that Enter/Space on a header toggles `aria-expanded` and the visibility of the controlled region, and that arrow keys move focus between sibling headers (WAI-ARIA accordion pattern).

findings.title: AdminDashboardModal and its compartment modals have no test files
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/tabs/dashboard/components/admin/UsersCompartment.svelte (4 aria/role hits per grep, zero tests)
findings.explanation: The entire admin dashboard FE — the surface owner/maintainer roles use to manage users, permissions, requests, reviews, releases — has no test files (no `tabs/dashboard/__tests__` exists). All of these are modal/drawer/popover overlays where focus trap, focus return, Escape-to-close, role=dialog, role=menu/listbox, and aria-expanded matter. RolePicker alone has 8 ARIA-attribute usages, yet there is no test asserting any of them.
findings.proposed_action: Add a `tabs/dashboard/__tests__/` directory mirroring the component layout. Minimum coverage per modal/drawer/popover: (1) dialog/menu role + aria-modal/aria-haspopup + aria-label, (2) Escape closes, (3) focus enters on open and returns on close (testable via Modal.test.ts helper), (4) Tab cycles within the surface, (5) aria-expanded toggles where applicable. Use a shared a11y test helper.

findings.title: CombinationPicker has no keyboard navigation or ARIA assertions
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/picker/__tests__/combination-picker.smoke.test.ts:116-209 (4 tests covering: row click emits selection, bucket head pill placement, claimer + ready badge overlay, no overlay without capability — zero keyboard or ARIA assertions)
inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/picker/CombinationPicker.svelte (per grep: 7 aria/role attribute usages in source)
findings.explanation: The picker is a list-style selection widget surfaced from the dashboard. The smoke test exercises only mouse clicks and visual grouping. It does not assert: (a) the rows expose `role="option"` or `role="button"` with discoverable labels, (b) Arrow keys move highlight, (c) Enter selects the highlighted row, (d) Escape dismisses, (e) Tab order is preserved against the filter rail. Keyboard-only users cannot reliably pick a reciter without testing these.
findings.proposed_action: Add `combination-picker.keyboard.test.ts`: after rows load, fire ArrowDown to move highlight, assert visual highlight class + `aria-selected`, fire Enter and assert the same `select` CustomEvent payload as a click, fire Escape and assert dispatch of close.

findings.title: prefers-reduced-motion media query gates exist in source but no test verifies the animation respects them
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/recitation-animation/__tests__/LineAnimation.char.test.ts:1-72 (only test in the directory; verifies cross-word co-timed letters — no matchMedia stub, no reduced-motion assertion)
findings.explanation: The recitation animation subsystem ships static-CSS reduced-motion handling, but the LineAnimation test stubs nothing on `window.matchMedia` and never asserts the reduced-motion branch is taken. A regression where someone removes the `@media` rule, or replaces a CSS transition with a JS-driven RAF animation that ignores the user's reduced-motion preference, would not fail any test. This matters for vestibular-disorder users following along with recitation.
findings.proposed_action: Add a test that stubs `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` to return matches=true and renders LineAnimation / AyahFilmstrip; assert that the active-character marker uses opacity/visibility transitions instead of `transform` translations (or whatever the reduced-motion branch's contract is). Pair the assertion with a small JS hook in source (e.g. `useReducedMotion()` rune) so the branch is observable from JS, not just CSS.

findings.title: No test asserts a live region / aria-live / role=status for state announcements (toasts, save status, claim updates)
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/stores/__tests__/ (only claim-confirm-modal.test.ts and editing-mode.test.ts — no toast/announcement coverage)
findings.explanation: The app surfaces async state changes (save success, claim acquired, validation results refreshed) through transient toasts. No test asserts the host carries `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` (or `assertive` for errors), so screen-reader users have no guarantee these announcements are spoken. There is also no ToastHost test file at all.
findings.proposed_action: Add ToastHost.test.ts: assert the container exposes `aria-live` (polite for info/success, assertive for error) and `role="status"`/`role="alert"` as appropriate; assert added toasts mount as descendants of the live region (so the SR re-announces). Separately verify that the save-flow store dispatches a toast whose text matches the visible message — protecting both visual and auditory channels.

findings.title: Modal.test.ts is misleadingly scoped — only tests close paths and scroll lock, not the "modal" contract
evidence: inspector/frontend/src/lib/components/__tests__/Modal.test.ts:6-72 (`describe('Modal', ...)` with 7 `it` blocks: render-when-closed, render-title-when-open, close-on-button, close-on-Escape, backdrop click, body scroll lock, restore on destroy)
findings.explanation: The describe-block name (`'Modal'`) implies the file tests the Modal contract. In practice it only exercises three close paths and scroll lock — it doesn't touch the dialog role, aria-modal, aria-label, focus trap, focus restoration, or Tab cycling. A new contributor reading the test list will assume the modal contract is covered; it is not. A more accurate `describe` name and a clear gap-test pattern (`it.todo` for the untested invariants) would prevent that misread.
findings.proposed_action: Either rename the describe to `'Modal — close + scroll lock'` to set scope expectations and add a second describe `'Modal — a11y (TODO)'` with `it.todo('traps focus on Tab/Shift+Tab')`, `it.todo('returns focus to previously focused element on close')`, etc. — or close the gap with real assertions per a11y-modal-focus-trap-untested.

findings.title: No HTTP-level test wires claim → save → mark-ready → publish → release for a single reciter
findings.explanation: Every leg of the canonical reviewer journey (claim → save edits → mark-ready → admin POSTs generate-timestamps → ts webhook publishes → released) is tested in isolation through a different fixture (state_persistence vs. tmp_reciter_dir vs. _seed_marked_ready). No test mounts the Flask test_client and drives the full chain on a single slug — so a drift between, e.g., what mark-ready persists into the claim row and what the webhook orchestrator (complete_timestamps_job) re-reads to publish is invisible to CI. test_state_parity.py covers cross-surface read parity for one mutation at a time, not multi-step lifecycle progression. test_timestamps_jobs.py::test_complete_publishes_marked_ready bypasses the HTTP layer entirely by directly seeding marked-ready via _seed_state.
findings.proposed_action: Add a single integration test in inspector/tests/routes/ (e.g. test_route_lifecycle_e2e.py) that uses signed_in_client + tmp_reciter_dir + state_persistence to: (1) POST /api/claim/<slug>, (2) POST /api/seg/save/<slug>/<ch>, (3) POST /api/mark-ready/<slug> with checklist, (4) POST /api/admin/generate-timestamps/<slug> (with stubbed launch), (5) POST /api/webhooks/ts-job-complete with the same secret/job_id, (6) assert /api/reciter-task/<slug> + /api/public/reciter/<id> agree the row is now released with no assignee. This pins the state-machine-meets-routes seam that today is implicit.

findings.title: No HTTP-level test chains POST /api/requests/intake → admin accept → POST /api/admin/intake/<rid>/ingest → auto_detect into a single flow
findings.explanation: The intake handoff documented in CLAUDE.md (intake submit → accept → ingest → auto_detect reconcile → AWAITING_REVIEW) is tested with three independent harnesses: (1) test_route_requests.py drives /requests/intake + accept but stops at status='accepted' with slug=None and never POSTs to /api/admin/intake/<rid>/ingest in the same test, (2) test_route_intake_ingest.py exercises the ingest route with a SQL-injected accepted-intake row (_seed_accepted_intake bypasses the route), and (3) test_intake_ingest.py::test_ingest_then_autodetect_flips_to_awaiting_review chains ingest+autodetect at the SERVICE layer but skips the route boundary entirely. A regression between intake_route's payload shape and intake_service's accept-shape contract is invisible to CI.
findings.proposed_action: Add an integration test that (1) signs in as contributor and POSTs /api/requests/intake with a real submission body, (2) signs in as owner and POSTs /api/admin/requests/<rid>/accept, (3) POSTs /api/admin/intake/<rid>/ingest with the per-delivery body, (4) drops a reciters/<slug>/detailed.json into tmp_path, (5) calls auto_detect.reconcile_once() (or the boot wrapper), (6) asserts /api/reciter-task/<slug> reports AWAITING_REVIEW with the pending-edit fields applied. This pins the actual JSON contract between FE-submission shape and intake_service.ingest body shape.

findings.title: released → unlocked-for-revision → re-claim → re-publish cycle is uncovered at any layer
findings.explanation: The state handlers _h_unlocked_for_revision (released → awaiting_review + RevisionContext stamped) and _h_unpublished (released → awaiting_review, RevisionContext cleared) have no dedicated tests at any tier. The grep for 'unlocked_for_revision' and 'reciter.unpublished' surfaces only capability/activity classification tests (string membership only) and the _services_smoke.py operator script which is not collected by pytest (filename underscore-prefixed; __init__.py is empty; pytest skips _*.py by default). So the second-claim cycle (released reciter unlocked, a contributor re-claims it, saves edits, re-publishes) — the entire 'revise a published reciter' user journey — is not exercised in CI. revision_in_progress field state transitions (set on unlock, cleared on republish, preserved across save) are completely unverified.
findings.proposed_action: Add inspector/tests/services/test_state_revision_cycle.py covering: (a) released → admin.unlocked_for_revision sets revision_in_progress with the correct unlocked_from_state/at/by, (b) released → reciter.unpublished clears revision_in_progress, (c) the full released → unlock → claim → save → mark-ready → republish cycle re-uses the same row, (d) capability gates (reciter.unlock_for_revision, reciter.unpublish) reject contributors/maintainers. Also add a route test for the unlock endpoint if one exists (or document the absence).

findings.title: POST /api/admin/cut-release has zero route tests despite being the final journey step
findings.explanation: The route module defines POST /api/admin/cut-release as the owner-only kick-off for the global GH release cut and the documented final step of the canonical journey (publish_hf → cut_gh). test_route_admin_releases.py covers /releases/status, /release-preview, and /publish-hf/<slug> but never POSTs cut-release. There is no test for: owner-only auth (release.cut_gh capability), single-flight rejection (cut_busy 409 check), payload validation, or the launch path. test_route_admin_releases.py docstring lists 'launch the global cut job' but the file has no matching test. test_jobs_base_staging.py tests stage_job_code but not the launch flow.
findings.proposed_action: Add tests in test_route_admin_releases.py for POST /api/admin/cut-release: (a) anonymous → 401, (b) contributor/maintainer → 403, (c) owner happy path with cut_release_jobs.launch stubbed → 202 + job_id surfaced, (d) when another cut_release job is in-flight → 409, (e) when no eligible released reciters → appropriate response. Also add an integration test that pre-seeds a released+ledgered slug then POSTs cut-release to verify the per-slug enumeration matches what /releases/status filtered in.

findings.title: test_route_admin_actions.py docstring claims state/force-set coverage but route and tests are both absent
findings.explanation: The docstring lists '/api/admin/{claim/force-release, claim/reassign, state/force-set, send-back, users/lookup}' but a grep across inspector/routes shows no state/force-set or state/force route exists and the test file has no test_state_force_set_* test functions. Either the route was removed and the docstring is stale (dead-test convention issue) or the route still exists somewhere and there is a real coverage hole. Either way, an agent reading the docstring expecting force-set coverage gets misled.
findings.proposed_action: Remove 'state/force-set' from the docstring on line 3 since no such route appears to exist. If admin force-set was intentionally retired, also update CLAUDE.md/docs/reference/admin-dashboard.md to remove references.

findings.title: Only 2 of the 3 documented request kinds are exercised; takedown and existing_combo_edit are uncovered
findings.explanation: The user task references 'the three request kinds (new, edit, takedown)' and the migration 0001 SQL comment lists 'existing_combo_edit|existing_reciter_new_combo|new_reciter|...' as supported request kinds. intake.py _INTAKE_KINDS is currently only ('existing_reciter_new_combo', 'new_reciter'); intake.py:225 and intake.py:337 reference 'existing_combo_edit' in comments but no code path or test handles it. There is no 'takedown' kind at all in the codebase. Either the kinds are formally out of scope (then docs/comments and CLAUDE.md should remove the references) or they are being prepared for but unprotected — a contributor adding a 'takedown' or 'existing_combo_edit' route today has no integration baseline.
findings.proposed_action: Decide and document: if the takedown/edit kinds are intentionally not built, remove the placeholder comments in intake.py:225+337 and the 'existing_combo_edit|...' enumeration in the migration SQL comment. If they're planned, add a registry of supported kinds with an assertion in tests/services/test_intake_ingest.py covering each kind's branch.

findings.title: inspector/tests/smoke/_services_smoke.py is the ONLY full-lifecycle integration but is filename-prefixed _ so pytest never runs it
findings.explanation: _services_smoke.py is the closest thing the repo has to an end-to-end integration: its docstring promises 'claim → mark-ready → unmark → release → claim → publish → timestamps → unlocked_for_revision → unpublished' and the body drives the full state cycle on a single slug. But (a) the filename begins with underscore so pytest's default test_*/Test_* collection skips it, (b) it defines smoke() rather than test_*-prefixed functions, (c) tests/smoke/__init__.py is empty (no collect_ignore handling). It runs only if a human invokes it manually. The 'smoke' for unlocked_for_revision lives only here — so the codebase's intended e2e is silent in CI.
findings.proposed_action: Either (a) port the smoke script's assertions into proper pytest functions split across test_state_*.py files (preferred — gets CI signal), or (b) explicitly run smoke as a pytest module by renaming to test_services_smoke.py and converting the smoke() body into multiple test_* functions sharing a per-module fixture. Document the chosen path in tests/README or conftest.

findings.title: auto_claim folding into alignment_completed has no HTTP-level test through /api/reciter/<slug>/request
findings.explanation: The user prompt flags auto_claim coverage as state-only. Confirmed: test_state_request_events.py covers auto_claim=True follow-up at the service tier (transition('reciter.requested', payload={'auto_claim': True})) but no route test verifies that posting {auto_claim: true} via the /api/reciter/<slug>/request HTTP body actually flows through to a UNDER_REVIEW row after auto_detect/alignment_completed fires. test_route_requests.py:128-146 only checks state='awaiting_alignment' immediately after submit. The skip-when-other-claim-held branch is similarly unprotected at the route layer.
findings.proposed_action: Add to test_route_requests.py an integration test that submits a request with auto_claim=True, fires the alignment_completed (via auto_detect.reconcile_once after dropping reciters/<slug>/detailed.json on the FilesystemBackend), and asserts the row ends at UNDER_REVIEW with assignee_hf_id set to the requester. Mirror for the skip path (requester holds another claim).

findings.title: POST /api/admin/publish-hf/<slug> launch-success path is tested only for the ledger-gate, not the launch outcome
findings.explanation: test_publish_hf_accepts_ledgered_slug stubs hf_publish_jobs.launch to return a stub dict but only asserts response 202 — it does NOT verify (a) what the route persisted into delivery_states/per_recitation_releases for the hf track, (b) that the in-flight tracker now reports this slug, (c) that a second POST while the job is in-flight is rejected with the right code. The 'release_canon vs route guess' tension in /releases/status (released-without-ledger filtered) has no companion test for publish-hf in-flight overlap with a second publish attempt.
findings.proposed_action: Extend test_publish_hf_accepts_ledgered_slug to assert in-flight bookkeeping and the persisted hf-track row. Add test_publish_hf_rejects_when_already_in_flight using _stub_jobs_api(in_flight=[{'kind':'hf_publish','slug':...}]).

findings.title: discard → undiscard → re-request cycle has only single-step coverage
findings.explanation: reject_hard sets DISCARDED (test_state_request_events.py and test_route_requests.py), undiscard restores PUBLIC (test_route_requests.py:378). But the loop 'discard → undiscard → submit a fresh request → alignment_completed' is not stitched together in either test file, so the round-trip of visibility_reason scrubbing + pending entry availability + AWAITING_ALIGNMENT gateability after un-discard is silent.
findings.proposed_action: Add a test in test_route_requests.py that performs the full discard → undiscard → POST /api/reciter/<slug>/request roundtrip and asserts a fresh pending entry materializes with visibility=public.

findings.title: test_route_admin_actions.py module docstring references _stub_persist pattern that no longer exists
findings.explanation: Docstring says 'Mirrors test_route_access_admin.py patterns: in-memory state replacement + persistence stubs'. The actual code uses _replace_state→_seed_state (SQLite substrate, NOT in-memory) and _stub_state_persist is a no-op kept only so call sites don't churn. New contributors will read this and try to maintain a long-dead pattern.
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite the docstring to reflect the post-cutover pattern: SQLite substrate via the autouse _substrate_db fixture, _replace_state to seed delivery_states + open_claim, _stub_hf_users to inject HfUser lookup results. Remove the _stub_state_persist no-op since it adds noise.

findings.title: _replace_state / _row helpers are copied verbatim across multiple route tests
findings.explanation: test_route_claims.py, test_route_admin_actions.py, and test_state_parity.py each define their own _row(...) + _replace_state(...) helper with subtly different defaults (default state, default assignee_login, etc.). conftest.py already exposes _seed_state via the seed_state fixture, but the wrapper '_row + _replace_state' convention got copy-paste-forked across three route tests rather than being promoted. This is exactly the duplicated-seeding-helper signal the audit calls out (especially BE: _replace_state(), _row(), _hf_user(), _stub_hf_users()).
findings.proposed_action: Promote a shared _row() helper + seed_rows fixture in conftest.py that wraps _seed_state with the route-test-friendly defaults. Migrate the three call sites to use the fixture. Same for _hf_user and _stub_hf_users which appear in test_route_admin_actions.py:58-78 and could serve test_route_access_admin.py as well.

findings.title: 'subscribe-friendly' test asserts a tautology, not subscription semantics
findings.explanation: The test labeled 'selectors return new array references on state change (subscribe-friendly)' calls `getChapterSegments(s1, 1)` and `getChapterSegments(s2, 1)` on two different state objects and asserts the results are not `===`. Because `getChapterSegments` is `ids.map(...).filter(...)` (segments.ts:92-96), it ALWAYS allocates a fresh array regardless of state changes. The test would pass even if the implementation ignored its `state` arg, so it does not test the claimed contract (`segmentsStore` derivation actually re-running on upstream change). It is the only test whose name claims subscription semantics, yet it tests nothing of the sort.
findings.proposed_action: Either rename the test to reflect what it does verify ('returns fresh arrays per call') OR rewrite it to subscribe to `segmentsStore`, count notifications, write `segAllData.set(...)` and `selectedChapter.set(...)`, then assert exactly N notifications fired in the expected order.

findings.title: Phase-1/3/4/6 'deferred' describe.skipIf blocks are permanently stale; all modules now exist
findings.explanation: Every test that uses the `loadOptional` pattern pairs a 'live' suite (`describe.skipIf(!mod)`) with a 'deferred' suite (`describe.skipIf(mod)` containing `it.todo('phase-N: ... not yet present')`). The point of the deferred block was to guarantee the suite went green during incremental phases. All referenced modules now exist on disk: `domain/registry.ts`, `domain/apply-command.ts`, `domain/identity.ts`, `stores/segments.ts`, `stores/chapter.ts`, `utils/validation/stale.ts`. The deferred blocks therefore NEVER run; they are pure refactor litter that bloats the test tree and gives a false 'todos exist' signal in the reporter.
findings.proposed_action: Delete every `describe.skipIf(<truthy-module>)('... (deferred)', ...)` block and its `it.todo('phase-...')`. The `loadOptional` indirection itself is also dead — all modules import cleanly — so the suites could be flattened to direct imports.

findings.title: loadOptional helper hides specifiers from Vite for modules that all exist
findings.explanation: `loadOptional` docstring says 'Vite by default refuses to bundle a dynamic import whose target file does not exist at config time' — i.e. it exists ONLY because phase-1/3/4 modules weren't present. Every consumer now dynamically imports a module that exists; the wrapper just trades static type safety for `any` and forces every test to `await` at module scope. It's purely vestigial.
findings.proposed_action: Replace `await loadOptional<any>('../../stores/segments')` with `import * as segmentsStore from '../../stores/segments'`. Delete `optional.ts`. Drop all `describe.skipIf(!mod)` guards.

findings.title: derivedEq has zero tests despite being the equality-skip backbone of the edit store
findings.explanation: `derivedEq` is the load-bearing wrapper that gates fan-out from the bundled `_editState` writable into 8 per-field readables (`editMode`, `editingSegUid`, `editingMountId`, `editingSegIndex`, `editCanvas`, `trimWindow`, `splitState`, `editStatusText`). Every SegmentRow subscribes to `$editMode` and `$editingSegUid`, so a regression that breaks the equality skip (e.g. accidentally allocating a new object in the selector) fans out N×rows×writes at 60fps. There are zero tests covering: (1) the prime-on-subscribe path (lines 40-48) when source changes mid-life, (2) identity-equal subsequent values being suppressed, (3) multiple late subscribers all getting the cached value, (4) unsubscribe cleanup releasing the source subscription.
findings.proposed_action: Add `inspector/frontend/src/lib/utils/__tests__/derived-eq.test.ts` covering: prime-on-subscribe sees current source value (not stale module initial), identical selector results skip emit, distinct selector results emit, multiple subscribers share one source subscription, unsubscribe drops the source link.

findings.title: segments/stores/playback.ts and timestamps/stores/playback.ts have zero subscription tests
findings.explanation: `setPlayingSegment` (playback.ts:141-154) is documented as identity-guarded for the 60fps rAF tick — same-pair sets must return the prior reference, and `origin` must inherit from the previous pair when omitted (the comment explicitly calls out the rAF advance tick scenario). No test exercises the origin-inheritance branch, the same-pair early return, or the null-coalescing default. `registerWaveformContainer` / `waveformContainer` action (lines 72-92) have no add/remove cleanup test. The entire `tsPort` / `tsPortReady` / `tsVbrChapters` surface has zero tests despite being read by the karaoke tick and the seek path.
findings.proposed_action: Add tests for `setPlayingSegment`: (a) same `{chapter, index, origin}` returns identical reference (no allocation), (b) update with `origin` omitted inherits previous origin, (c) null clears, (d) different chapter/index allocates new object. Add tests for `registerWaveformContainer`: add+returned-cleanup removes from set; double-register stays a set.

findings.title: All three Svelte 5 rune stores (releasesStore, reviewsStore, adminDashboard) have zero tests
findings.explanation: The three `.svelte.ts` rune stores are the codebase's first migration off `writable`/`derived` toward `$state` + getter-derived. They carry non-trivial state — `reviewsStore.open()` (lines 68-82) does a Set immutable-copy mutation, fires `markReviewViewed` best-effort, and is the cross-store coordination point. `releasesStore.toggleFacet` (releases.svelte.ts:47-49) round-trips the active-value clear. `adminDashboard.openModal` (admin-dashboard.svelte.ts:32-35) sets two `$state` fields atomically. None of these have a test — so neither the rune semantics nor the contract (refreshSeq monotonicity, getter-derived `hasActiveFilters` reactivity, set-mutation-with-assign-back pattern) is pinned.
findings.proposed_action: Add `inspector/frontend/src/lib/stores/__tests__/releases.svelte.test.ts`, `reviews.svelte.test.ts`, and `inspector/frontend/src/tabs/dashboard/stores/__tests__/admin-dashboard.svelte.test.ts`. Cover: filter clears reset all axes, `toggleFacet` clears on second call with same value, `hasActiveFilters` flips with filter mutations, `refreshSeq` increases monotonically, `reviewsStore.open` (mocked `markReviewViewed`) records to `viewedThisSession` only once per slug, `close()` clears selection + drawer, `adminDashboard.setUnviewedRequests(-5)` clamps to 0.

findings.title: isAdmin / isOwner / capabilities derived stores untested
findings.explanation: `isAdmin`, `isOwner`, and `can(id)` are the FE's dashboard-level authz gates (documented as 'Mirrors services/permissions.is_maintainer'). They have NO direct tests — coverage is incidental via the `editing-mode.test.ts` calls of `syncEditingMode`. `markGuideReadLocally` (current-user.ts:106-111) is anonymous-guarded and idempotent; the guard is untested. `loadCurrentUser` swallows fetch errors and resets to anon; the error path is untested.
findings.proposed_action: Add tests for `isAdmin`/`isOwner` reacting to role changes via `currentUser.set`, `can('x')` recomputing only when capability set membership flips, `hasCapability` for null/undefined user, `markGuideReadLocally` no-op for anonymous and dedup for signed-in.

findings.title: shuffle store localStorage load + auto-persist subscribers untested
findings.explanation: shuffle.ts has TWO module-load side effects: (a) `load(LS_SHUFFLE_*)` reads localStorage to seed writable initial value, (b) two `.subscribe()` calls that auto-persist every change. The existing test does `localStorage.clear()` in beforeEach AFTER the module has already loaded, so it never exercises the load path. It also never verifies persistence — `cycleShuffle()` is called, but `localStorage.getItem(LS_SHUFFLE_AYAH)` is never asserted. The `exitLoop()` side effect on transitions 0→1 and 1→2 (shuffle.ts:70, 75) is also unverified.
findings.proposed_action: Use `vi.resetModules()` + manipulate `localStorage` BEFORE re-importing to test the seed path. Assert `localStorage.getItem(LS_SHUFFLE_AYAH) === 'true'` after `cycleShuffle()`. Mock `exitLoop` and assert it fires on 0→1 and 1→2 but not 2→0.

findings.title: Module-load localStorage subscriptions persist across all tests in the same file
findings.explanation: The two top-level `shuffleReciter.subscribe(...)` / `shuffleAyah.subscribe(...)` calls fire on every `.set(...)` for the entire test process lifetime, including across the `beforeEach` `localStorage.clear()`. So the `.set(false)` in beforeEach immediately re-writes `'false'` into localStorage. The test never controls for this; if other tests in the same process expected fresh-localStorage state for these keys, they'd see the residue. `playback.ts` and `autosave.ts` have similar module-load localStorage reads but no test isolation.
findings.proposed_action: Either (a) tear down the module via `vi.resetModules()` per test, or (b) document that these module-level subscribers cannot be undone and require a clear teardown order. The shuffle-store contract test should explicitly assert both directions: set → localStorage written, localStorage primed → store seeded.

findings.title: lib/playback/loop.ts (loopTarget + exitLoop) has no tests despite being the cross-tab loop authority
findings.explanation: loop.ts is re-exported by `tabs/timestamps/stores/playback.ts` and consumed by both segments and timestamps tabs (cycleShuffle calls `exitLoop()` on transitions). The `lib/playback/__tests__/` directory tests audio-port, audio-graph, audio-range — but never loop.ts. This is the cross-store coordination glue and breaks would silently let loop survive shuffle activation.
findings.proposed_action: Add `inspector/frontend/src/lib/playback/__tests__/loop.test.ts` covering: loopTarget set/get round-trip, exitLoop nulls loopTarget, exitLoop on already-null is a no-op, subscribe-set-set delivers only the latest distinct value when implementation uses equality skipping.

findings.title: dashboard-state, submit-wizard, catalog-data stores untested
findings.explanation: `dashboard-state.ts` defines a discriminated `DashboardView` union ({kind:'list'} | {kind:'detail',reciterId,...}) plus `activeFilters: Record<string, Set<string>>` with a Set-mutation-via-assign-back pattern (`toggleFacet`). The Set immutability pattern is the exact one called out as load-bearing on the Svelte 5 reactivity boundary in `reviewsStore.open`. Zero tests verify `toggleFacet` actually clears when re-toggling the same tag, that opening detail preserves filters, that closing detail restores list view, or that the `openRequest` flag is consumed exactly once.
findings.proposed_action: Add `inspector/frontend/src/tabs/dashboard/stores/__tests__/dashboard-state.test.ts` covering view transitions, facet toggle add/remove, filter persistence across view transitions, sort/search round-trip. Similar coverage for submit-wizard and catalog-data.

findings.title: edit.ts bundled-state fan-out optimisation untested
findings.explanation: edit.ts explicitly documents the contract: 'a write that changes only one field does NOT fan out to subscribers of the other seven' (lines 6-10). This is critical because hundreds of SegmentRows subscribe to `$editMode` and `$editingSegUid`. The setters (`setEditingSegIndex`, `setEditCanvas`, `setEditStatusText`) skip-update when value is identical (the `s.X === x ? s : {...s, X}` pattern). No test verifies: (1) `setEditCanvas(canvas)` does NOT fire `editMode` subscribers, (2) identity-equal setter calls produce zero subscriber notifications, (3) `clearEdit()` resets all 8 fields atomically (single store write).
findings.proposed_action: Add `inspector/frontend/src/tabs/segments/stores/__tests__/edit.test.ts` that wires `editMode`/`editingSegUid`/`editCanvas`/`editStatusText` subscribers with notification counters, then asserts: `setEditCanvas(c)` increments only editCanvas counter; `setEditStatusText(same)` increments nothing; `setEdit('trim', uid, mountId)` increments mode+uid+mountId but not canvas/trimWindow.

findings.title: segValidation derived stores (accordionViewActive, splitGroupIndex) untested
findings.explanation: `accordionViewActive` is documented as 'mutually exclusive' with chapter cards and gates `<SegmentsList>` render. `splitGroupIndex` falls back to `{}` on null validation. Neither derivation, nor `clearValidation()`'s multi-store atomicity (resets `segValidation`, `valUiOpenCategory`, `valUiScrollTop`), is tested. These are the validation panel's reactive backbone.
findings.proposed_action: Add tests: `accordionViewActive` flips on `valUiOpenCategory.set('category')` and back to false on null; `splitGroupIndex` returns `{}` when validation is null and the server map when present; `clearValidation()` triggers exactly one notification per consumer.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md references a docs/planning/svelte-migration.md that doesn't exist
evidence: CLAUDE.md (Conventions section: 'migrated either opportunistically when touched for a feature, or in dedicated batches per docs/planning/svelte-migration.md')
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md commits a contributor to follow `docs/planning/svelte-migration.md` for the rune migration plan and lists 'TimestampsWaveform.svelte and the canvas/audio-imperative components' as indefinitely-legacy 'see the plan doc for the indefinitely-legacy list'. The `docs/planning/` directory does not exist in this repo (only `docs/reference/`). A new contributor auditing test gaps against the Svelte 4 vs Svelte 5 migration plan has no plan doc to consult — the prompt itself was asked to look there.
findings.proposed_action: Either (a) add `docs/planning/svelte-migration.md` listing the migration order and indefinitely-legacy file list, or (b) move the plan content into `docs/reference/frontend.md` and update CLAUDE.md's reference. Without one of these, the 'don't mix syntax in the same file' convention is a floating rule with no exemption list to check against.

findings.title: compat.test.ts throws inside skipIf-gated `it` blocks instead of using skipIf properly
findings.explanation: Inside `describe.skipIf(!chapterStore)('compat shape', ...)`, every `it` block does `if (!segmentsStore) throw new Error('phase-4: stores/segments not yet present')` — but the outer `skipIf` only checks `chapterStore`, not `segmentsStore`. If `chapterStore` resolved but `segmentsStore` failed to resolve (asymmetric phase), the suite would throw instead of skipping. With both modules present today the branch is dead, but the gate is logically wrong and silently passes only because of the current file layout.
findings.proposed_action: After deleting the deferred blocks (per stale-phase-skip finding), inline-import both modules and drop the `if (!mod) throw` ladder. The skip-if-missing dance is no longer needed.

findings.title: expected/registry-snapshot.json is orphaned: no regenerator, no consumer, and already stale
findings.explanation: The 175-line JSON file expected/registry-snapshot.json is committed to the repo but is referenced by zero code paths: a repo-wide grep for `registry-snapshot` matches only the file itself. Neither snapshot_expected_outputs.py nor snapshot_route_baselines.py produces it, and the FE parity test at frontend/src/tabs/segments/__tests__/registry/parity.test.ts:14 inlines its own `PY_SNAPSHOT` literal rather than loading this file. The orphan is already stale: it lists 11 issue kinds (failed, missing_verses, missing_words, structural_errors, low_confidence, repetitions, audio_bleeding, boundary_adj, cross_verse, qalqala, muqattaat) while the live Python registry (registry.py:62-206) has 13 — `low_confidence_v2` and `basmala_amin` were added but the snapshot was never re-generated because nothing regenerates it. Either it's a forgotten Phase-1 artifact (regenerator was removed before this commit) or it was meant to be loaded by the FE parity test and never wired up. Either way the file rots and misleads new contributors who diff it against `registry.py` to learn the registry shape.
findings.proposed_action: Decide: (a) delete the file outright (preferred — FE parity test already has its own snapshot), or (b) add a regenerator (e.g. a function in snapshot_expected_outputs.py that dumps `dict(IssueRegistry)` to the file) AND change the FE parity test at parity.test.ts:14 to load it via the `@fixtures` alias instead of duplicating the literal. If (b), also register a CI drift gate on the file (same pattern as schema-codegen-check).

findings.title: snapshot_route_baselines.py patches RECITATION_SEGMENTS_PATH on 5 of 7 modules that don't have it
findings.explanation: The regenerator subprocess (lines 78-88) walks 7 module paths and conditionally sets `mod.RECITATION_SEGMENTS_PATH = _reciter_root` on each. Only 2 of those 7 modules actually define a module-level `RECITATION_SEGMENTS_PATH` attribute (`services/storage/data_loader.py` and `services/activity/history_query.py`). The other 5 (routes.segments.data/edit/validation, services.segments.save, services.segments.undo) read storage paths via `services/storage/data_dir.py` and `storage_paths.py` (per CLAUDE.md's bucket-first reads invariant), so the `hasattr` guard silently skips them. The regenerator is effectively running against the real `INSPECTOR_DATA_DIR=/tmp/...` injection and not the per-module patching it pretends to do. If the data_loader / history_query indirections ever stop honoring `INSPECTOR_DATA_DIR` (e.g. switching fully to bucket-mounted reads), the regenerator will silently capture *production* baselines mixed with empty tmp data — without error.
findings.proposed_action: Replace the module-list-walking hack with a single call to the data_dir facade. Either (a) set `INSPECTOR_BACKEND=filesystem` + `INSPECTOR_DATA_DIR=$tmp` and let services/storage/data_dir.py route reads to tmp the same way the test fixtures do, or (b) reuse the existing `tmp_reciter_dir` pytest fixture pattern from conftest.py:420 instead of forking a subprocess. The current module-patching loop is a stale remnant from a pre-services/storage layout and gives a false sense of isolation.

findings.title: expected/<fixture>.routes.json baselines captured 6 weeks ago against commit 4be27a3, behind 13+ validation/route commits
findings.explanation: The baseline pins `captured_against_commit: 4be27a3` and `captured_at_utc: 2026-04-25T14:48:39Z`. Since then 13+ commits have touched `inspector/services/validation/` (e.g. 4392c8db basmala_amin gate, b4c0429f is_wasl + cross_verse rework, bcfb266b basmala_amin ignorable) and `inspector/services/validation/classifier.py` has had 4 changes. The MUST-1 superset contract means tests will still pass as long as no field is removed — but the baseline no longer reflects what `/api/seg/validate` actually returns today (it omits `low_confidence_v2` and `basmala_amin`), so it tests progressively less of the surface. No CI gate forces re-capture after a real API change, and as established in finding `snapshot-route-regenerator-patches-nonexistent-attrs`, the regenerator is partly broken so running it is risky. There is no SHA staleness check (compare `_meta.captured_against_commit` to HEAD) that would warn a reviewer the baseline is months old.
findings.proposed_action: After fixing the regenerator, re-capture and commit fresh baselines so `field_keys_top_level` includes `low_confidence_v2` and `basmala_amin` (the validate route's actual current shape). Long term: add a tiny pytest test that warns (xfail or skipif annotation) when `_meta.captured_against_commit` is more than N commits behind HEAD on the validation/routes paths — surfacing drift without breaking CI.

findings.title: pytest.importorskip("services.validation.classifier", reason="phase-2 — unified classifier not yet introduced") is stale; module exists
findings.explanation: test_classify_per_category.py:11 unconditionally calls `pytest.importorskip("services.validation.classifier", reason="phase-2 — unified classifier not yet introduced")` at module load. The classifier module exists at `inspector/services/validation/classifier.py` and is imported throughout the codebase (e.g. `services/validation/snapshot_classifier.py:16`), so `importorskip` succeeds — the skip is dormant. But the reason string still claims phase-2 hasn't landed, which is incorrect and misleads anyone debugging a future test failure (they will believe the module is missing). The same stale reason text persists in `snapshot_expected_outputs.py`'s docstring ("Run after Phase 2 lands the unified classifier") and the comment about "Pre-Phase-2 the script raises ImportError" — neither is true anymore. Phase-2 has landed and the import resolves at script collection time.
findings.proposed_action: Drop the `importorskip` call (line 11) — direct imports inside the test bodies are sufficient and will fail loudly if the module is ever removed. Update the snapshot_expected_outputs.py docstring to remove Phase-2 phasing language; reword to simply "regenerate the per-fixture classifier baselines".

findings.title: test_validation_identity.py has 4 stale phase-6 importorskips plus a test pinned to a ghost worktree name
findings.explanation: Lines 38, 53, 68, and 81 call `pytest.importorskip("services.validation.detail", reason="phase-6 — ...not yet present")`. The module is present and the three referenced helpers (`resolve_segment_by_uid`, `resolve_segment_for_issue`, `filter_stale_issues`) all exist (detail.py:490, 502, 532). The skips are dormant but reason strings are dishonest. Worse, lines 97-114 (`test_no_index_fixups_after_phase_6`) walks up `__file__` looking for a directory literally named `inspiring-ramanujan-2d4e7e` — a defunct worktree slug. That walk hits the drive root, then `edit_dir` becomes `<DriveRoot>/inspector/frontend/src/tabs/segments/utils/edit` which does not exist on any other contributor's machine or in CI. `os.walk` yields zero files, `leaks` stays `[]`, and the test passes vacuously — it never actually asserts that `_fixupValIndicesFor` has been deleted from any source file.
findings.proposed_action: Remove the four stale `importorskip` calls and convert them to direct imports. Rewrite the repo-root resolution in `test_no_index_fixups_after_phase_6` to use a stable anchor: `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]` (3 parents up from `inspector/tests/identity/`) or check for a sentinel like `pyproject.toml`/`.git`. Verify the test actually catches a planted `_fixupValIndicesFor` reference before landing.

findings.title: Only the FE-types codegen has a CI drift gate; routes.json and classify.json baselines have none
findings.explanation: `schema-codegen-check` (.github/workflows/inspector-checks.yml:78-111) regenerates `inspector/frontend/src/lib/types/generated/schemas.ts` on every CI run and `git diff --exit-code`s it — that closes the writer/reader drift loop for the FE types. No equivalent gate exists for `expected/*.routes.json` (regenerated by `snapshot_route_baselines.py`) or `expected/*.classify.json` (regenerated by `snapshot_expected_outputs.py`). Both regenerators ship in-tree with `python -m` entry points but the workflow never invokes them, so a developer can refactor validation output without re-capturing baselines and nothing breaks until manual review. Combined with `snapshot-route-regenerator-patches-nonexistent-attrs` (routes regenerator is broken anyway) and `routes-baselines-12-commits-stale` (currently 6 weeks behind), this is the root infrastructure gap that allowed both findings to develop.
findings.proposed_action: After fixing the routes regenerator, add a `parity-baseline-check` job that (1) runs both regenerators against the committed fixtures and (2) `git diff --exit-code`s the `expected/` directory. The classify baselines are deterministic from the fixtures + classifier code, so this gate works cleanly. The routes baselines record `_meta.captured_at_utc` and `_meta.captured_against_commit` which would diff on every run — strip those from the diff comparison or move them to a sibling sidecar file.

findings.title: Snapshot regenerators live under inspector/tests/parity/ instead of scripts/codegen/ where CLAUDE.md says they should
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md's `Conventions` section pins operational CLIs to `scripts/<function>/` (codegen, bucket, backfills, etc.) and the scripts-layout-guard CI job (`inspector-checks.yml:117`) enforces no `inspector/scripts/` directory. The repository has exactly one regenerator that lives where it's supposed to (`scripts/codegen/regen_fe_types.py`), and two more (`snapshot_route_baselines.py`, `snapshot_expected_outputs.py`) hiding under `inspector/tests/parity/` with `python -m inspector.tests.parity.snapshot_expected_outputs` entrypoints. They are operational regenerators (write committed JSON), not tests — they're invoked from documentation, not collected by pytest. Hiding them in the test tree makes them invisible to anyone scanning `scripts/codegen/` for codegen tooling, which is where a new contributor would expect to find them.
findings.proposed_action: Move both regenerator modules to `scripts/codegen/regen_route_baselines.py` and `scripts/codegen/regen_classifier_baselines.py`. Keep import logic to load fixtures from `inspector/tests/fixtures/segments/`. Update READMEs and the docstrings to reflect the new paths. The pytest tree should contain assertions over baselines, not the writers of baselines.

findings.title: No test asserts that running the snapshot regenerators twice produces identical output
findings.explanation: Both regenerators claim idempotence (snapshot_expected_outputs.py docstring: "Idempotent.") but neither is asserted. A test that ran the classifier regenerator twice against the same fixture and compared the byte output would (a) catch non-determinism in `classify_entry` (dict iteration order, set ordering in `categories`), (b) catch regenerator bugs that swallow exceptions, and (c) close the loop for the proposed CI drift gate. The route regenerator can't be tested for byte-idempotence because `_meta.captured_at_utc` is recomputed every run — that itself is a smell.
findings.proposed_action: Add `tests/parity/test_regenerator_idempotence.py` that imports `snapshot_expected_outputs.regenerate("112-ikhlas")`, captures the bytes, calls it again, and asserts byte-equality. For the route regenerator, factor out the timestamp-stripping into a helper so the test can compare the stable portion. This is the prerequisite for finding `no-drift-gate-on-routes-baselines`'s CI gate.

findings.title: No golden/snapshot baseline for the edit_history.jsonl record shape; only inline-dict round-trip tests exist
findings.explanation: There is exactly one `.edit_history.jsonl` fixture in `inspector/tests/fixtures/segments/` and no expected/golden file pinning its decoded shape against the `EditHistoryBatch`/`EditHistoryOp` schema in qua_shared/schemas. Per CLAUDE.md's shared-schemas invariant, both the offline extraction pipeline and the Inspector save flow MUST round-trip these artefacts through Pydantic models — yet there is no snapshot that demonstrates a real fixture is accepted by the current model. test_peaks_history_schema.py covers `PeaksRecord` round-trip via inline dict literals (good), but the per-batch `edit_history.jsonl` shape (batches, ops, targets_before/targets_after) is not pinned anywhere. If `EditHistoryBatch` adds a required field, the inline tests still pass and the fixture silently rots until a real production load fails.
findings.proposed_action: Add `expected/112-ikhlas.edit_history.json` capturing the Pydantic-validated form of the existing `112-ikhlas.edit_history.jsonl`, write a test that loads the jsonl, runs each record through the canonical parser, and asserts equality against the golden. Wire the regenerator into a `scripts/codegen/regen_history_baseline.py` so the same drift gate from `no-drift-gate-on-routes-baselines` covers it.

findings.title: audio_manifest schema has no snapshot or fixture-backed round-trip test
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md's bucket-shape section pins `catalog/audio_manifest/<slug>.json` as a per-reciter source artefact, and the shared-schemas invariant requires round-trip through the Pydantic model. Grep for `audio_manifest|AudioManifest` returns only routes-handler test files (`test_audio_meta.py`, `test_intake_ingest.py`, `test_route_peaks.py`, `test_route_intake_ingest.py`); none of them ship a fixture audio_manifest.json, none of them write a golden baseline through the Pydantic model. If the schema evolves (e.g. adds a `cbr_bitrate_kbps` field), live bucket files are untested and the FE-types codegen would catch only the TS-side change, not whether existing on-disk audio_manifests still load.
findings.proposed_action: Add `inspector/tests/fixtures/audio_manifest/<slug>.json` capturing a real-world manifest shape, plus `tests/persistence/test_audio_manifest_schema.py` that round-trips it through the canonical Pydantic model. Include a forward-compat case (extra field on disk) to prove `ConfigDict(extra="allow")` is honored.

findings.title: Stale 'Phase N' narrative language litters parity scripts and tests, contradicting the comments rule
findings.explanation: `.claude/rules/comments.md` explicitly forbids "refactor/cleanup" language: "no longer", "phase", "removed", "deleted", "deprecated". Yet every `pytest.importorskip` reason in this subsystem still says "phase-N — surface not yet present" or "phase-2 — unified classifier not yet introduced" — language that aged out of relevance 6+ weeks ago when those phases landed. The `_meta.policy` field in routes baselines also encodes phase narrative ("post-Phase-2 unified classifier").
